analysis.title: Up and Adam (Friday, November 20, 2026)
key_insights: The S&P 500 is on track for its steepest weekly decline since April 2025 (-5.1%) and sits 8.2% below its Oct. 6 record high. The report notes the average annual max drawdown is about 13%.

Consensus estimates point to 16% EPS growth in 2027, and the NTM P/E has fallen to its lowest since 2023. The report calls this an attractive entry point. The 14-day RSI is 31, near oversold, so the weakness may be technically overdone.

The S&P 500 Industrials sector fell a sixth consecutive day, its longest losing streak since 2024, and is 13.5% below its Aug. 14 record high. The steepest declines are in AI-buildout industries: Electrical Equipment (-25.6%), Construction & Engineering (-23.1%) and Machinery (-18.6%).

The report stays constructive on Industrials and calls the selloff overdone. It expects data center construction and related grid upgrades to continue, with lower oil prices as a further tailwind, despite potential regulatory headwinds.

Goldman Sachs' Financial Conditions Index (equity valuations, interest rates, credit spreads, US dollar) is at its highest level since May 2025. The report says markets may already be doing some of the Fed's work.

Fed Chair Warsh has repeatedly said financial conditions were too easy. He acknowledged some tightening since the Fed's September rate hike but stopped short of calling conditions restrictive, and the report says that may be changing.
US investment grade corporate issuance is above $190b month-to-date, the fifth monthly record of 2026. Year-to-date issuance is above $2t, an all-time high, partly driven by hyperscaler borrowing.

IG spreads held at 86-92 bps in November despite the supply. IG total returns are -0.6% MTD and +1.6% QTD, versus 0.0% QTD for high yield and -6.2% for the S&P 500. The report expects issuance to ease into year-end, supporting spreads, and favors higher-quality bonds with index yields near 6%.

A typical Thanksgiving dinner for 10 costs about $59 in 2026, up 6% YoY and the first annual increase since 2022. Turkey rose most (+10%), and the Farm Bureau ties the rise to higher diesel and fertilizer costs. The meal is still about 9% below its 2022 all-time high.

Prior-day close (11/19): S&P 500 -2.0% to 7,176, Dow -2.2%, Nasdaq 100 -2.2%, Russell 2000 -2.2%. Premarket futures show S&P 500 -0.8%, Nasdaq 100 -1.7%. The only listed event is final Michigan Sentiment at 10:00am, consensus 51.0, prior 51.0.

sector_views.rationale: The report is constructive and calls the six-day selloff overdone. It expects data center construction and grid upgrades to continue, with lower oil prices as a tailwind, despite regulatory risk.

earnings_insights: Consensus estimates point to 16% EPS growth for the S&P 500 in 2027 (estimate, not a reported figure).

macro_indicators.interpretation: Scheduled for 10:00am ET today. The consensus equals the prior reading, so the market expects no change.
Tighter conditions from equity valuations, rates, credit spreads and the dollar act like additional policy tightening, which the report says may be doing part of the Fed's work.
First YoY increase since 2022, driven by diesel and fertilizer costs. It is a reminder of inflation pressure in food.
Spreads are stable despite record issuance.

risk_factors: Potential regulatory headwinds for AI-related data center construction, which is driving the Industrials selloff.
Tightening financial conditions, with the Fed under Chair Warsh having raised rates in September.
Record IG bond supply, including hyperscaler borrowing, if issuance does not ease into year-end.
Higher agricultural input costs (diesel, fertilizer) feeding food inflation.
